category_title: Highly reserved and anxious students with significant writing avoidance
minimal_context: The class is participating in a read-aloud discussion of mythical characters in Eric Carle’s poetry collection, Dragons, Dragons.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to have a read-aloud discussion about mythical characters in Eric Carle’s poetry collection, Dragons, Dragons. Everyone please gather for the group.

STUDENT: (Sits in the back of the group, fiddling with books on the shelf, and rarely looking up.)

TUTOR: Please pay attention to the reading.

STUDENT: (Faces away during the discussion, keeping her head down on her desk and squirming.)

TUTOR: Do you have anything you want to add about the characters?

STUDENT: (Continues facing away and staring into space, not speaking a word to the group.)

options.A: Talk informally with the student about the various poetry collections they have read recently during the read-aloud session.
options.B: Enlist the whole class to validate the student's action using thumbs up, and socially identify the behavior as something authors do.
options.C: Use an interactive reading app where every single word of the poem flashes up on the screen during the discussion.
options.D: Make available diverse genres on a range of relevant topics from which the student can choose, including graphic novels, poetry, and biographies.
